x-jsf-presentation.description:
We offer optional supplemental health plans through OSDE and Swiss Medical, also known as "Prepagas" which include coverage for the employees and their eligible dependents.
Important: In Argentina, the healthcare system is financed by mandatory social contributions from both employers and employees. Employees contribute 3% of their gross monthly salary up to a regulatory cap, while employers add 6% without any cap. Even if you opt to offer a private plan ("Prepaga"), "you must still make these contributions, which employees can direct towards the healthcare plan and provider of their choice.
x-jsf-presentation.extra:
The majority of this benefit cost is already covered by the existing mandatory social program contributions from both employer and employee each month. The final cost of the plan will depend on whether the total plan cost surpasses the contributions collected in Remote’s shared pool. If there is an excess, it will be evenly distributed among all customers within the same tier, promoting fairness and transparency in cost-sharing
</br>
Prices are listed in USD, local currency equivalent will be determined based on exchange rate at the time of invoicing.
</br>
Please note that all local payroll deductions for required coverages are included in the Cost Calculator.
</br>
Pricing listed is subject to change based on age of the employee (age banding) and/or plan changes/renewals. Any pricing updates will be communicated in advance of updated billing.
</br>
Important: All employees should choose an Obra Social at Onboarding stage.

statement.description:
If you need Remote to terminate a post-probation employee in Argentina because of your company’s economic or organizational circumstances, a mutual termination agreement must be entered into with the employee.

During probation, you have some more flexibility on termination; for example, when the termination reason is the employee’s performance. For this reason, we recommend setting the probation period to the maximum allowed.
